title: Overdue Explanations of Benefits and the Credit on an Insured Plan of Care
content:
On an Insured Plan of Care, visits whose explanation of benefits is overdue are covered by a hold on the credit standing on the plan.

**Which visits count.** A visit counts here when at least one but fewer than three whole calendar months separate its date of service from today, it is not an initial evaluation, and no coinsurance charge and no non-covered service charge has been posted for it.

**What is held.**

| Visits that count | Held from the credit |
|---|---|
| None | Nothing |
| 1 | $20.00 |
| 2 | $40.00 ($20.00 for each) |
| 3 or more | The whole credit |

The overdue-explanation hold is **$20.00 per visit** for one or two such visits. The amount held is taken off the credit together with any other amount held back from it, and what remains is never below zero.

## Questions and answers

**Does a visit from last week count?** No. Fewer than one whole calendar month separates it from today.

**Does a visit exactly three whole calendar months back count?** No. It must be fewer than three whole months back. With today 2026-06-15 (hypothetical), a visit dated 2026-03-16 is two whole months back and counts; one dated 2026-03-15 is three whole months back and does not.

**Does the initial evaluation count?** No, an initial evaluation never counts here.

**What takes a visit out of the count?** A coinsurance charge or a non-covered service charge posted for it.

**Hypothetical case.** Today 2026-06-15; treatment visits dated 2026-04-02 and 2026-04-09 have no coinsurance and no non-covered charge; a visit dated 2026-04-20 carries a coinsurance charge. Two visits count, so $40.00 is held.
